# SunBot Robotics Programming STEAM Education

> Robotics and coding education for children in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada.
> Classes run in the Terwillegar area of southwest Edmonton.
> Programs are organized for ages 6-10 and 9-14. SunBot's general model caps classes at six students.
> In regular class work each student usually has their own robotics kit; for major challenge
> projects and competitions students work in teams of 2-6.

This file is an experimental, informal summary of public pages. It is not required by any
search engine or AI provider. The authoritative sources are the HTML pages, robots.txt and
sitemap.xml.

## Identity

- Website name: SunBot Robotics Programming STEAM Education
- Google Business Profile and Google Maps listing: SunBot Kids Robotics & STEM Education
- Short brand name: SunBot
- Founder and lead instructor: Adam Sun
- Public profiles: Google Maps, Instagram (@sunbot_edmonton), Nextdoor

## Programs

- FLL Explore, ages 6-10. Beginner. No prior experience required. LEGO Education WeDo or
  SPIKE Essential, programmed with drag-and-drop icon blocks. Guided building, simple
  programs, teamwork, and a local showcase presentation. Maximum 6 students.
- FLL Challenge, ages 9-14. Intermediate to advanced, beginners accepted. LEGO SPIKE Prime
  or MINDSTORMS EV3, programmed with Scratch-based block coding; the platform also supports
  Python. Autonomous robot missions, innovation project, Core Values, and registration for
  local and regional FIRST LEGO League Challenge events. Maximum 6 students.

Pricing listed on course pages: CAD $40 per hour. Promotions are handled by inquiry.
Materials and LEGO Education kits are provided in class.

## Key answers for common parent questions

- Best starting age: around 6-7 for introductory robotics, if the child can follow building
  steps with guidance. SunBot accepts children from age 6.
- Prior experience: not required. Ages 6-10 (FLL Explore) start with icon drag-and-drop
  on WeDo or SPIKE Essential. Ages 9-14 (FLL Challenge) start with Scratch-based blocks
  on SPIKE Prime or EV3. Classes capped at six students.
- Robotics or coding first: for children under about 10, robotics generally makes
  programming concepts concrete faster because feedback is physical.
- Explore vs Challenge: Explore is an introductory, showcase-based division for ages 6-10.
  Challenge is a judged competition division for ages 9-14 with autonomous robot missions,
  an innovation project and Core Values.
- Teenagers: SunBot teaches up to age 14. Students 15 and older should look at senior FIRST
  programs or high-school robotics clubs.
- Trial classes: yes. Book by emailing sunbotcanada@gmail.com or texting +1 780 655 0833
  with the child's age. No camp schedule is published on the website; ask directly.
- Enrollment: email sunbotcanada@gmail.com, text +1 780 655 0833, or use the contact form,
  including the child's age.

## Learning focus

Hands-on building, programming, engineering challenges, problem solving, teamwork,
presentations and project-based learning, using LEGO Education robotics kits.

## Location

Street address: 157 Hayward CR NW, Edmonton, AB T6R 3G2, Canada
Terwillegar area of southwest Edmonton, near Terwillegar Community Recreation Centre.
The recreation centre is a nearby landmark only; classes are held at the Hayward CR address.

## Service area

Southwest Edmonton, Alberta. Communities served include:

- Terwillegar and Riverbend area: Hodgson, Riverbend, Terwillegar Towne, Terwillegar
  Gardens, Magrath Heights, Haddow, Falconer Heights, Rhatigan Ridge, Brookview,
  Bulyea Heights, Ogilvie Ridge, Carter Crest, Grandview Heights
- Windermere and Keswick area: Windermere, Ambleside, Keswick, Langdale,
  Glenridding Heights, Glenridding Ravine
- Heritage Valley and Rutherford area: Rutherford, MacTaggart, Heritage Valley,
  Heritage Valley Town Centre, Chappelle, Desrochers, Allard, Cavanagh, Paisley,
  Graydon Hill
- South Edmonton: Ellerslie, Summerside
